calls.reason: Sightline confirms 190 GW of announced capacity, but provides no comparable annual demand measure or OpenAI–Anthropic spending share. The claimed ratio and concentration remain unestablished.

Reports document substantial Meta and Jane Street commitments, but give neither market-wide customer shares nor hyperscalers' end uses. They also cannot settle the companies' long-term ability to pay.
CoreWeave reported a $740 million quarterly loss, while Nebius's net profit included investment gains. These consolidated results do not establish profitability across AI data centers generally.

CBRE reports unleased capacity under construction, and Build Technologies identifies speculative AI campuses without disclosed tenants. SemiAnalysis also describes long-term commitments as dominated by AI labs, supporting the main point.

CBRE's strong preleasing and low vacancy challenge the demand concern, but describe earlier market conditions. The packet lacks sustained payment and utilization evidence from the construction pipeline after commissioning.
